# v0.29.1-rc3 — a restart after a cleanup pass no longer stores the conversation again

This is the third release candidate for v0.29.1, a patch release on v0.29.0; it follows v0.29.1-rc2. **Changes since rc2** are listed first; the rest of these notes cover everything since v0.29.0. rc2's reference-agent window found a restart storing a whole conversation a second time; this candidate fixes that, and nothing else changed. v0.29.1 fixes three compaction problems found in v0.29.0's release testing: passes that could not cut past a row the host still holds, the 10-minute pause after such a pass ending early, and summaries that could read a leaf's rows out of store order after a host reorder. It also stores a re-stamped tool turn after a cold restart, makes the doctor's local-recall messages clearer, and fixes links in the install payload.

There are no new settings, the schema version stays 5, and v0.29.0 remains the latest stable release until this candidate passes its gates (see **Qualification**).

## Changes since rc2

- **A restart after a cleanup pass no longer stores the conversation again.** A compaction pass that only cleans up the host's list (it swaps a large stored message or tool output for a short stub, or strips reasoning, and writes no summary) kept its record of the cleaned list in memory only. After a restart, LCM-X had no current record of that list, so it could fail to match the host's list and store rows it already held a second time; a message later stored out of order broke even an older record the same way. rc2's reference-agent window stored 291 rows a second time like this; nothing was lost. The record is now saved when the host commits the cleaned list, but only when that list replays the conversation since the last compaction: each distinct message stored since then needs its own entry in the list, and every message in the list must already be stored. A cleaned list that holds only new messages keeps its record in memory, as before. LCM-X also rewrites the saved record to match the host's current list in three cases: after a message is stored out of order, after it reconciles a batch of messages the host saved, and at a restart whose list it recognises as a replay of a session that already holds rows (for example, after an earlier version left the record stale). A restart whose first list holds only new messages does not rewrite it. A message stored in the form LCM-X replays it (a redacted tool result, for example) counts as stored, and the rewrite keeps every earlier-session row that a later summary still has to cover. If a message the record would mark as stored is not in the store, or the rewrite fails, the old record stays: that can still duplicate a message but never hides one. One narrow case on hosts that send only new messages is listed under **Known issues**. v0.29.0 has the same problem ([#1286](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1286), [PR #2114](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2114)).
- **Two retry shapes after a compaction store exactly once.** Retrying the last message after a compaction and a cold restart, or retrying a message sent right after a compaction, could store the summary text, merged into a user message, a second time at the next restart. The same record rewrite now keeps both to one copy ([#1446](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1446)).

### Testing improved since rc2

- 54 new restart tests, 35 of which fail on rc2; two others record a known limit ([#2124](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2124), under **Known issues**). Regression tests cover the two retry shapes above, which rc2's own suite records as known failures. The new tests include:
  - the reference agent's order of events: a published compaction, then a committed cleanup pass, then a message changed among later turns;
  - the first restart after an upgrade from a version that left the record stale;
  - lists that hold only new messages, with or without the system prompt in front;
  - repeated replies and turns, and a session holding an older version's duplicate copies;
  - rows stored in their replayed form;
  - a failed record rewrite;
  - a session started by a compaction.

  The exactly-once state machine now also tries retries next to a merged summary. The trace goldens record the rewrite, including at a cold restart ([PR #2114](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2114)).
- **Upgrade probe:** sessions were given a stale record the way v0.29.0 leaves one, then restarted twice, with and without redacted rows. In all 8 cases, the second restart on this candidate stored only its own new turn and no message a second time. v0.29.0 stores already-stored messages again at every restart.

## Changes since v0.29.0

### Compaction

- **Compaction gets past an unresolved retained row.** When the stored history before a row the host still holds could not be cut, every compaction pass made no progress. Compaction now summarises the blocked rows from the stored copy, up to the leaf budget, and moves on. The host's copy stays in context, so its content can appear twice but is never lost. This also works when the row sits in the protected recent turns or behind a backlog larger than one leaf, the two cases where v0.28.1's bounded escape failed. A leaf now ends before a tool group whose other half the host keeps. Each pass that uses this escape logs one WARNING naming the stored rows (IDs, role and kind only), and the `LCM compaction stop` line gains an `escaped=` field ([#1162](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1162), [#1880](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1880), [PR #2003](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2003)).
- **Compaction keeps going after the session rotates.** In rc1, the record of rows compaction had summarised past a retained row (the escape below) belonged only to the session that wrote it. After a compaction rotated the session, the new session no longer recognised the host's copies of those rows, so every later compaction pass stopped with `selected leaf chunk lacks raw store lineage` for the rest of the conversation. The new session now also reads the records of the sessions it was compacted from (only verified compression parents, never an unrelated or forked session), so compaction keeps making progress. Stored rows were never lost. This affected rc1 only ([#2027](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2027), [PR #2028](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2028)).
- **The 10-minute pause after a pass that changes nothing holds again.** In v0.29.0 the pause ended as soon as any new message was stored, so the next turn could run another 10–73 s pass. The running engine now waits the full 600 s, as v0.28.1 did; a restarted engine still reads the saved pause record. That record now tracks only this session's messages and summaries, so activity in another session no longer ends it. Forced, overflow, recovery and survival-ceiling compactions never wait ([#1880](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1880), [PR #2002](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2002)).
- **Summaries read a leaf's rows in store order after a host reorder.** When the host moved a stored row later in its view, the summariser could read one leaf's rows out of store order, so an older fact could follow its correction inside a summary. The summariser now reads them in store order, with each tool call before its results; a reused tool-call ID is matched by store order. Which rows a leaf covers is unchanged, and stored rows are never reordered ([#2007](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2007), [#2011](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2011), [PR #2012](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2012)).

### Restarts and retries

- **A re-stamped tool turn after a cold restart is stored.** After compaction and a cold restart, if a host that gives messages no unique IDs re-sent the last assistant/tool pair with new timestamps, LCM-X could treat the pair as a retry of the stored copy and not store it. It now refuses that match when the pair's own known timestamps differ, the same rule it already applied to message IDs. This was found in an engine-level test; a trace of the supported Hermes hosts found no path that produces it ([#1967](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1967), [PR #1969](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1969)).

### Doctor and install

- **Clearer local-recall readiness.** `lcm_doctor` reports local recall as ready, preparing or unavailable, keeps model faults apart from coverage read errors, shows catch-up progress as information and a stalled or failing catch-up as a problem to act on, and names the enable command when the companion is missing. While the model is not ready, recall's `degraded` reason is one short readiness sentence; the detail stays in the doctor. A model preparation that has used up its retries tries again only from the existing background triggers, with a bounded backoff ([#1959](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1959), [PR #1976](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1976)).
- **Install payload links.** Documentation links in doctor and embedding messages use the release's version tag and fall back to `main` when the version is unknown. The payload's README drops links to pages missing from its source commit and lists them in the manifest, and the link check resolves links from the page that contains them ([#1960](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1960), [PR #1977](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1977), [PR #1985](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1985)).

### Testing improved

- **Pinned-host suites:** the pinned-host fixture loads each host's real profile helpers, which clears the 12 per-host failures reported in the v0.29.0 notes; the catalog-scanner install test expects each host's own scanner verdict, and launcher paths with spaces are tested ([#1968](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1968), [#1975](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1975), [PR #1972](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1972), [PR #1979](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1979)).
- **Reliability matrix:** CI keeps and uploads each cell's re-score inputs, and the offline re-score refuses cells it cannot decide and scores stopped-turn cells ([#1987](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1987), [PR #1988](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1988), [PR #1991](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1991)).
- **Benchmark instruments:** older release trees are measured with the current instruments; benchmark producers are fixed for the local-recall default; the D1 local-recall arm gets a shared embedding cache, parallel shards and fixes for interrupt and kill races ([#1959](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1959), [#1971](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1971), [PR #1965](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1965), [PR #1973](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1973), [PR #1974](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1974), [PR #1980](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1980), [PR #1981](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1981)).
- **Release gates:** patch releases now run the gauntlet rows their diff selects ([#1995](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1995), [PR #2008](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2008)), and the D2 facts-kept row replays a run once when the summariser service, not the product, failed ([PR #2009](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2009)).

## On by default in this release

Every change above is on by default with no new setting. Local semantic recall stays on by default, as in v0.29.0.

## Upgrade

- **Host:** Hermes 0.21.3 or newer is still required (0.21.5 or newer recommended), with Python 3.11 or newer.
- **Store:** the schema version stays 5, with no new tables, columns or triggers. The compaction escape records hashes for up to 256 rows per session in the existing session metadata (when a session started by a compaction records its own escape, it stores its compression ancestors' entries with it, within the same 256-row cap); v0.29.0 does not read that record.
- **Settings:** none added, removed or changed.
- **From v0.28.1:** follow the v0.29.0 upgrade notes first. Local semantic recall turns on at that upgrade unless you set `LCM_EMBEDDINGS_ENABLED=false`.
- **First restart after the upgrade:** a session whose saved record went stale under an earlier version (for example, a committed cleanup-only pass with no compaction since) can store its already-stored messages once more at the first restart on this version. When that restart's list replays the session, LCM-X rewrites the record to it, so later restarts do not repeat it. The old record stays when a message it would mark as stored is missing from the store. On a host whose messages carry no timestamps, LCM-X cannot recognise the replay at a restart, so the repeat can continue until the next saved record, as on v0.29.0 (see **Known issues**). Nothing is lost.
- **Rollback:** target `v0.29.0`. Take a SQLite-safe backup first (see `docs/operator-guide.md`), and compare ordered raw messages and summary provenance through upgrade, rollback and re-upgrade.

## Known issues

- **Some compaction passes still write no summary** ([#1880](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1880)): with the escape above, a pass that stalled on a retained row now writes a summary. A pass that still forms no summary input (a tool group the host keeps half of, a contiguity stop, or rows with no stored source) writes no summary but still returns a rebuilt copy of the host's list, which the host commits. Returning the host's original list on such passes waits for a measurement on the reference agent. Nothing is lost.
- **Survival-fit rotations leave no compaction record:** when a session rotates because the survival fit trimmed the live view, the new session gets no record of what the previous one compacted, so rows stored under earlier sessions may not be matched to their stored copies. A compaction that is already blocked on such rows can then stay blocked, and while it is blocked each survival fit trims older rows from what the model sees with no summary in their place (in the rc1 case fixed above, some of those rows were not yet summarised). It was seen only together with that rc1 problem; its frequency on its own is unknown. No stored rows are lost: the store keeps every row and recall can still reach them. A fix is tracked for v0.30.0 ([#2029](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2029)).
- **Slow summaries can shrink the live view:** when summary calls time out at the compaction threshold, the survival fit can drop about 80–115 older rows from what the model sees. The store keeps every row and recall can still reach them; a fix is tracked for v0.31.0 ([#2004](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2004)).
- **Catalog install on upstream Hermes with the plugin scanner:** the upstream catalog entry pins the v0.28.1 payload until a catalog update to this release's payload lands; it is proposed after this release. Until then, a catalog install gets v0.28.1; use `scripts/install.sh` for this release. This release's payload is rated `caution` (not `safe`) because the small-host CPU detector reads `/proc`; nothing was changed to hide that from the scanner, and an upstream allowance is requested ([#1946](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1946)). Hermes 0.21.3's scanner blocks a `caution` verdict from a community source, so a catalog install there needs `--force` after reviewing the findings, or `scripts/install.sh`.
- **Upstream Hermes manual `/compress`:** on current upstream Hermes main, a manual `/compress` from the gateway uses the host's own compressor and bypasses LCM-X, so stored history can gain duplicate replies. No rows were lost in the reported cases. A fix is proposed upstream ([Hermes #143587](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/143587)); an LCM-X defence is planned for v0.30.0 ([#1922](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1922), [#1924](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1924)).
- **Retry shapes still being fixed** (all are redesigned together for v0.30.0, including the two cases that can lose a row, #1837 and #1838):
  - after a tool call is retried with new message IDs, each later cold restart can store that call and its result again: one more copy per restart, nothing lost ([#1836](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1836));
  - after a cold restart, if only the tool result's message ID changes on a retry, the new result may not be stored ([#1837](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1837));
  - if the plugin restarts before a session's first compaction and the host re-sends the last tool turn with a new timestamp on its user message, that user message and its tool pair may not be stored ([#1838](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1838));
  - in some retry and restart sequences after compaction, a replaced or retried message can be dropped or stored twice ([#1451](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1451)).
  Real-host frequency is unknown.
- **Crash before a reply, then rotation:** on hosts that do not give messages unique IDs, if the agent crashes before replying and the conversation then rotates, the next turn can be stored twice. The v0.28.1 notes planned this fix for v0.29.0; it now targets v0.30.0 ([#1508](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1508)).
- **Duplicates kept on purpose:** turns stored before v0.29.0's carried-stamp marker can be stored again by a replay, and user messages that the host itself mirrors after an ACP crash recovery are kept twice. LCM-X keeps both copies rather than risk losing a genuine message; see `docs/identity-ledger.md` ([#1501](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1501), [PR #1775](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1775)).
- **Replays can store rows a second time:** when a host replays rows that carry no timestamps, tool results and replies that are already stored can be stored again, as on v0.28.x. Nothing is lost, but recall can show the row twice; a fix is planned for v0.30.0 ([#1674](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1674)).
- **A crash right after a rotation can keep an extra reply:** after such a crash, LCM-X can store an assistant reply that the host never made durable, so it holds one reply more than the host. Nothing is lost; this shape predates v0.29.0 and appeared intermittently in one reliability cell ([#824](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/824), [#861](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/861)).
- **Local embeddings on large, fully embedded stores (small hosts):** on a 2-CPU host with a 250,000-row fully embedded store, a semantic recall could use its full 8-second budget. Since v0.29.0, hosts with at most 2 effective CPUs answer from full text immediately when local embeddings are on by default (`degraded=true`, `cpu_limited`); explicit settings keep control. Faster exact semantic recall under contention is tracked in [#1586](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1586); the first attempt did not meet its memory bar, so no release is promised yet.
- **Local embeddings can outvote exact keyword hits:** with v0.29.0's deep-match fix, recall with embeddings off now returns its full 25 matches as well, and on the LoCoMo benchmark it answers more questions than the default local embeddings (1,165 vs 1,089 of 1,986 questions). Fusion gives the keyword arm half the weight of each embedding arm, so embedding-only hits can push an exact keyword hit out of the 25. Local embeddings still lead on LongMemEval-S (426 vs 408 of 500) and show no regression against v0.28.1. A fusion-weight change needs its own measurement and is planned for a minor release, not this patch ([#950](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/950)).
- **Python only: switching an existing config object to a cloud provider:** if code changes `embedding_provider` to a cloud provider on an `LCMConfig` that already resolved to the local default (with `dataclasses.replace` or attribute assignment), the enabled setting carries over, and that provider starts receiving text without `embeddings_enabled=True`. Settings from the environment and new `LCMConfig(...)` objects are not affected. Set `embeddings_enabled` explicitly when you switch providers in code; a fix is tracked in [#1959](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1959).
- **Subagent work is not stored:** what a delegated subagent does in its own session, including its tool calls and intermediate results, is not stored by LCM-X. Only what the subagent returns to the parent conversation is stored, so `lcm_recall` cannot find a subagent's intermediate results. This isolation is not new in this release. Storing subagent sessions is planned for v0.30.0 ([#1931](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1931)).
- **A restart at an unlucky moment around compaction can store one summary row again** ([#1286](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1286)): three narrower restart timings stay open. They are a restart after a cleanup-only pass that the host kept without signalling that it committed it; with the non-default `compression.in_place=false`, a restart after the host published the new session but before LCM-X saw it start; and a restart while a second compaction still waits for the host to adopt it. Each can store the summary text once more as a message. Nothing is lost, and all three are older than v0.29.0.
- **A repeated message on a host that sends only new messages** ([#2124](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2124)): the saved record above counts identical messages once, so a cleaned list that carries every distinct message since the last compaction, but fewer copies of a repeated one (a reply like "Done." given twice), is treated as a replay of the conversation. On a host that sends its full history at each turn, as the reference agent's host does, the same list after a restart is a replay, and storing nothing is correct. On a host that sends only new messages, a message can be lost in one narrow case: after a compaction, a batch of new messages that repeats every distinct message stored since that compaction can be taken for a replay and not stored. Telling the two apart needs a record of which stored rows are duplicates, planned for v0.30.0.
- **Hosts whose messages carry no timestamps:** LCM-X recognises a replay at a restart only from timestamped messages. On such a host, a message inserted earlier in the list, or a list of only new unstamped messages, can still be stored again at each restart, as on v0.29.0. Nothing is lost. The reference agent's host timestamps its messages.
- **Restart duplicates the fix does not cover yet:** in a few rarer orders of events the saved record is not rewritten, so the next restart can store messages a second time, as on rc2; none loses a message ([#2115](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2115), [#2119](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2119)). When a host replaces an unstamped reply during a resend, or edits an unstamped assistant message in place, the new text is stored only at the next restart, along with a second copy of the conversation ([#2116](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2116), [#2117](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2117)).
- **Summary obligations after an out-of-order row in a session started by a compaction:** a later summary may not be required to cover some of the parent session's messages. The messages stay in the store and recall can still reach them. This predates v0.29.0; a fix is tracked for v0.30.0 ([#2123](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2123)).
- **Cross-process cleanup:** another process sharing the store can still clear an empty live session binding and stall later compaction ([#753](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/753), [#761](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/761)).
- **Extra rows in one degraded mode:** when a child compaction can never publish, three runtime hosts store extra rows and repeat user tags. No user content is missing. That reliability cell now gates on missing content only ([#1797](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1797), [#1900](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1900), [PR #1929](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1929)).

## Qualification

This is a release candidate for testing. It is not qualified for general use yet, and v0.29.0 remains the latest stable release. As a patch release, v0.29.1 runs the gauntlet rows its diff selects ([#1995](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1995)). rc2's gauntlet found the problem fixed above (the reference-agent window), and the fix changes how messages are stored, so every selected row runs again on this candidate. Where the release rules allow, rows reuse v0.29.0's baseline measurements from the rc2 runs; each receipt says so. The GA notes will report each row below with its receipt.

- D1 recall changes in the shipped local default, with embeddings off recorded beside it: **TBD**.
- D4 question answering in the local default, D8 delivery guards and the A/A′ placebo: **TBD**.
- D2 facts kept, D3 Track S absolutes and D7 per-message wait: **TBD**.
- D5 reference-agent window and the D5-B controlled clone: **TBD**.
- Occurrence grader, the #1586 same-store local recall row and the offline-model recall check: **TBD**.
- Not run: the D6 recorded rows (not selected for this patch).
